what: A test that a crate with records runs no resolution, expansion or item-tree query cannot be written against a fixture database: setting the crate graph resolves every crate from source at once (the name-resolution maintainer's pass), before anything can give the database a record. It is F2 in a test's clothes: the store is asked last.
cost: the restart test of the lane's brief is not written; the lane's tests show that a served crate answers alike and reads few pages, not that nothing was resolved
cause: the maintainers run in the write that makes the crates, and a served crate is told apart only by an input set afterwards
whys: why at the write: a reader must never find a crate unmaintained
why is served-ness set afterwards: an image's key needs the crate graph, which that write makes
why not keyed in the same write: `deps::keys` reads the database (source roots, crate data), so it needs the write done
class: an order fixed by who needs whose output, where the cheaper answer (a record) is only askable after the dearer one (resolving) was computed
prevention: restore.md F2: the lowering's batch keys every crate and asks the store before its maintenance pass, a crate whose key is not known yet stays unmaintained with a reader of it an error; then the count test (`Counts::executed` by crate) is the guard
